[audio:preop-interview#s003] (PROVIDER, 29.2-37.2s) Thank you. Now, let's review your medications. Your records list amlodipine, metformin, and atorvastatin. Are you still taking all these?
[audio:preop-interview#s004] (PATIENT, 37.6-43.6s) Amlodipine and atorvastatin still taking every day, doctor. But metformin... stopped already one year plus.
[audio:preop-interview#s005] (PROVIDER, 44.0-47.2s) Metformin was stopped? Can you tell me why?
[audio:preop-interview#s006] (PATIENT, 47.6-56.0s) Yes, doctor. My sugar level very good on diet alone. HbA1c last check was 6.2%, so doctor say can stop metformin.
[audio:preop-interview#s007] (PROVIDER, 56.4-62.4s) I see. We'll update your records. Any allergies? Your file mentions penicillin causes a rash.
[audio:preop-interview#s008] (PATIENT, 62.8-68.4s) Yes, doctor. Once take penicillin, body get red spots. Never take again after that.
[audio:preop-interview#s009] (PROVIDER, 68.8-73.2s) Noted. Have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?
[audio:preop-interview#s010] (PATIENT, 73.6-79.6s) No, doctor. Wife make sure I NPO from last night. Only sip water for meds.
[audio:preop-interview#s011] (PROVIDER, 80.0-84.4s) Good. Any previous surgeries or anesthesia? Any problems during those times?
[audio:preop-interview#s012] (PATIENT, 84.8-91.2s) Had gallbladder out ten years back. Anesthesia okay, wake up no problem. No dizziness or vomiting.
[audio:preop-interview#s013] (PROVIDER, 91.6-96.0s) Excellent. Finally, how's your mobility now? Can you walk with assistance?
[audio:preop-interview#s014] (PATIENT, 96.4-103.2s) Can walk short distance with cane, but pain very bad. Need help for stairs or long walks.
[audio:preop-interview#s015] (PROVIDER, 103.6-110.8s) Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with spinal anesthesia and propofol sedation as planned. Any questions for me?
[audio:preop-interview#s016] (PATIENT, 111.2-114.8s) No, doctor. All clear. Thank you for explaining everything.

These clarification questions were raised in gap analysis; ensure the note answers each one (or records it as unresolved):
- Is the patient still taking aspirin?

Cover the standard ASA elements as sections: History, Medications, Allergies,
NPO status, Airway exam (only as dictated), ASA-PS (with justification claims),
and Plan. Each claim:
- text: one atomic fact.
- section: which element above.
- provenance: the id(s) of the supporting chunk/segment, exactly as bracketed.

current but the patient says they stopped it), state the CURRENT truth from
the interview and cite it; do not silently keep the stale record value.

resolved conditions (a pneumonia cleared years ago, a healed fracture),
long-discontinued medications, and incidental items with no anesthetic
implication. Before writing any claim from past history, apply this test:
would this item change the anesthetic plan, airway management, drug choice,
or post-op monitoring? If no, leave it out entirely. If yes,
state that reason in the claim text (e.g. "... — relevant because ...");
a historical item without a stated anesthetic reason does not belong here.

    }

  ],
  "title": "WriterOutput",
  "type": "object"
}
